f.title: Set up collection protocols that capture literature suggesting lack of effectiveness for approved indications
f.statement: MAHs are required to appropriately collect the safety management information stipulated by Article 7 of the GVP Ordinance by setting up Protocols on Collection of Safety Management Information that provide how to collect literature or other articles suggesting that marketed drugs or active ingredients do not demonstrate effectiveness for approved indications in clinical trials, preclinical trials and other findings.
f.clause: Notes 1. Collecting research reports suggesting that drugs do not demonstrate effectiveness for approved indications
f.applicability: Drugs marketed in Japan by MAHs subject to the GVP Ordinance (MHLW Ministerial Ordinance No. 135 of 2004); English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)
f.systems: Protocols on Collection of Safety Management Information
f.processes: Safety intake & collection; Local PV interfaces

f.title: Collect safety management information from overseas companies for same-ingredient overseas drugs
f.statement: MAHs should collect safety management information from overseas companies if there are drugs used overseas that are ascribed to contain the same ingredients as the drugs manufactured by the MAHs ("overseas drugs").
f.clause: Notes 2. Prompt collection of information from overseas companies
f.applicability: MAHs whose drugs have same-ingredient drugs used overseas; English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)
f.processes: Partner & vendor oversight; Safety intake & collection

f.title: Agree in advance with overseas companies how and by when safety information is exchanged, and write it into the collection protocols
f.statement: MAHs manufacturing drugs that have overseas drugs should appropriately collect the safety management information stipulated by Article 7 of the GVP Ordinance by determining in advance with the overseas companies the ways of obtaining and transmitting safety management information and the time deadlines for providing information, and by including these procedures in the Protocols on Collection of Safety Management Information under Article 5-1-1 of the GVP Ordinance.
f.topic: Safety data exchange with overseas companies
f.clause: Notes 2. Prompt collection of information from overseas companies
f.legal_basis: GVP Ordinance Art. 7; GVP Ordinance Art. 5-1-1
f.applicability: MAHs whose drugs have same-ingredient drugs used overseas; English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)
f.systems: Protocols on Collection of Safety Management Information
f.processes: Partner & vendor oversight; Safety intake & collection

f.title: Promptly submit to PMDA information that a new overseas safety measure (labeling or CCSI revision) is under review
f.statement: If MAHs learn that a new additional safety measure (e.g. revision of the labeling of an overseas drug, or revision of the company core safety information [CCSI] of drugs used internationally) is under review, the MAHs should promptly submit the information to the PMDA.
f.clause: Notes 2. Prompt collection of information from overseas companies
f.applicability: MAHs whose drugs have same-ingredient drugs used overseas; English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)

rows.deadline: Promptly, once the MAH learns the measure is under review

f.title: Review the need for Japanese safety measures, including package insert revision, before the overseas measure is finalised
f.statement: MAHs are also required to review the necessity of an additional safety measure, including revision of package inserts in Japan, concurrently, before a safety measure including labeling revision is finalized overseas.
f.clause: Notes 2. Prompt collection of information from overseas companies
f.applicability: MAHs whose drugs have same-ingredient drugs used overseas; English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)

f.title: MAH determines seriousness of ADRs conclusively, even if the reporting doctor considered them non-serious
f.statement: MAHs are responsible for determining the seriousness of ADRs conclusively, even if the reporting doctors considered that the ADRs were non-serious.
f.clause: Notes 3. Consideration of necessity for reporting Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs)
f.applicability: Adverse drug reaction reports obtained from medical facilities; English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)

f.title: Assess seriousness comprehensively: symptoms, overall status, underlying and concomitant diseases, outcome
f.statement: MAHs should comprehensively determine the seriousness of reported ADRs, considering symptoms and overall status, underlying and concomitant diseases, and outcomes of patients.
f.clause: Notes 3. Consideration of necessity for reporting Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs)
f.applicability: Adverse drug reaction reports obtained from medical facilities; English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)

f.title: Ensure data-processing system upgrades, in-house and at outsourcing contractors, do not disrupt ADR processing
f.statement: MAHs should ensure that updated programs following upgrading of data-processing systems do not affect data-processing, not only in their own companies but also in outsourcing contractors, in order to process information on ADRs appropriately.
f.topic: System upgrades and outsourced data processing
f.clause: Notes 4. Management when upgrading of data-processing systems
f.applicability: MAHs processing ADR reports in-house or through outsourcing contractors; English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)
f.processes: Validation & change control; Partner & vendor oversight
